library.title: Why did the search miss the notice?
library.subtitle: Trace the Saturday question through candidate selection and claim support.

beats.title: Read the dated question
beats.explanation: The request is about application-help availability on Saturday, 21 November. Search must keep both the service and date in view.
beats.keyIdea: A passage without its date or service scope may sound relevant while answering the wrong question.
beats.narration: The visitor asks about application help this Saturday. The search needs both the service and the dated schedule. Opening hours alone answer a different question.

beats.title: Retrieve current candidates
beats.explanation: The current public notice, service page, and opening hours appear in the candidate set. The earlier notice remains stored but is superseded and ineligible.
beats.keyIdea: Stored, eligible, retrieved, and selected are separate stages.
beats.narration: The current hybrid search returns the dated notice, service page, and hours. The older notice is still archived but does not qualify for this answer.

beats.title: Narrow the candidate set
beats.explanation: Switch the authored search to hours-only candidates. The current notice disappears from retrieval before any answer is written.
beats.keyIdea: A retrieval miss happens before reranking or context assembly.
beats.narration: Now the search uses only the hours-focused candidates. The decisive current notice never enters this list. The answer cannot verify Saturday application-help availability from the remaining passages.

beats.title: Try to rerank
beats.explanation: Reordering the four returned candidates cannot create the missing notice. The source still exists in records, but the answer does not receive it.
beats.keyIdea: Reranking sorts candidates; it does not perform a new retrieval.
beats.narration: Try sorting the retrieved cards. Their order can change, but the missing notice cannot appear. A new retrieval strategy is needed.

beats.title: Restore the evidence path
beats.explanation: Return to current hybrid retrieval. The notice becomes eligible, retrieved, and selected again; the suspension claim regains direct passage support.
beats.keyIdea: Repair the upstream candidate set, then inspect the specific claim and passage.
beats.narration: Restore the current hybrid search. The notice returns as a candidate and enters the selected context. Its exact passage supports the suspension claim. Nothing here books a visit.

service-counter.title: When does a slot become a booking?
service-counter.subtitle: Follow a typed calendar lookup, proposal, and timeout without inventing an action.

beats.title: Validate the lookup
beats.explanation: The public workflow checks application-help slots for Tuesday, 24 November. The request names a date and service; the lookup is read-only.
beats.keyIdea: A typed request establishes what is being checked, not what has been reserved.
beats.narration: The service worker checks Tuesday the twenty fourth for application help. The request has a typed date and service. Reading calendar availability does not book anything.

beats.title: Read available times
beats.explanation: The authored calendar response returns two Tuesday options at its checked time. These are possible times, not guarantees that availability will persist.
beats.keyIdea: A successful read-only result supplies options, not a completed write.
beats.narration: The calendar responds with two possible Tuesday times. This is a simulated snapshot of availability. It has no booking confirmation.

beats.title: Propose one time
beats.explanation: Move the first checked time to a proposal card. The visitor can review it, but the simulation has no booking write or confirmation.
beats.keyIdea: Proposed is a distinct action state from confirmed.
beats.narration: The worker proposes ten o clock on Tuesday. A proposal card is useful, but it does not reserve a slot. The booking state remains not booked.

beats.title: Encounter a timeout
beats.explanation: A later read-only check times out. The earlier proposal is cleared; fresh Tuesday availability is unknown. The interface must not retain a misleading success cue.
beats.keyIdea: A failed lookup must be reported as unknown, not converted into a booking or a claim of no slots.
beats.narration: The next calendar check times out. No fresh slots are verified, and the earlier proposal disappears. This is unknown availability, not an empty schedule and not a booking.

beats.title: Explain the action boundary
beats.explanation: Compare the successful lookup and the timeout. Neither includes an authorized booking write, operation ID, or confirmation result.
beats.keyIdea: Only an explicit successful confirmation could justify booked language; this case never executes one.
beats.narration: The first response offered a possible time. The later response timed out. Neither completed a booking. The honest next step is to check again or hand off, not to imply success.
